stages.title: The Mission
body: Run the café for invited staff
Use your role. Check, serve, clear down.
Open only when the adult says ready.
stages.notes: Untimed. Source: sources/MTP.xlsx; revision sha256:0895674f2901b602daf998b8a7aa1516522ce0c301b23bfba941fcc1807977cd. Medium Term Plan!D9; Lesson register!F13. This is a supervised real cold-food service with practice payment only. Before food handling or opening, the responsible adult confirms the approved recipe and actual ingredient labels, written allergen information, clean suitable equipment and handwashing facilities, the agreed food-storage and service plan, the venue and supervision. Hair is tied back, watches and jewellery are removed as required by the adult’s hygiene procedure, and phones stay away from the food area. The Mission also needs invited staff, approved cold items and practice money ready. Learners do not decide whether a food is suitable for an allergy. If any check is unresolved, do not prepare or serve that item: stop and refer to the responsible adult. Follow the setting’s food-safety procedures. Keep practice-money and food roles separate; wash and dry hands again before food handling after money, phones, cleaning, waste or touching hair/face. An unready session may rehearse with empty pots and cards, but must be recorded as rehearsal, not the completed practical or live-service outcome.

stages.title: Arrival task
body: Opening reminders: check with the adult; count stock.
Name your two opening checks.
What does clear down mean?
What is our agreed stop signal?
Why say thank you to a customer?
BLUE / GREEN / AMBER / RED. Choose a pause or quiet station.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. Self-contained reminders and role prompts are supplied. Check each learner’s actual role card without assuming previous teaching. Expected clear-down: put away and clean under the adult’s plan. The adult agrees and rehearses the actual stop signal with each learner individually before opening; no universal signal is assumed. Thank you acknowledges the customer politely. BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer a brief pause or quieter station without public disclosure. Agree one return action privately. The adult takes over any food task or service position while a learner pauses.

stages.title: Our service standard
body: Repeat each order before the handover.
Is that right?
Agree the stop signal with the adult.
If unsure, stop and ask.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Revisit one concrete service standard: accurate repeat-back. Adult checks that each learner understands the locally agreed stop signal and the return action. Use the quieter preparation station if needed; do not require front-of-house performance.

stages.title: Run the opening checks
body: Confirm your actual role and two opening checks.
Count the actual opening stock.
Count the practice float together.
Rehearse the agreed stop signal.
Open only after the adult confirms readiness.
stages.notes: 5 minutes. Run checks together; record actual opening stock and float, not the worked example. Adult confirms the approved cold menu, ingredient/allergen record, storage/use plan, equipment, venue, invited staff and supervision. A fresh approved batch may be needed. Check actual item quantities and record them. Training float is £2 + £1 + £1 + 50p + 50p = £5, but actual values remain blank until counted. After counting practice money, wash and dry hands before handling food. Keep practice-money handling and ready-to-eat food preparation in separate agreed roles. A person who touches practice money or a phone, cleans, handles waste or touches hair/face washes and dries hands again before food handling. The adult checks this before any role switch.

Greet, repeat, hand over and serve as agreed.
Use the order record and practice money only. Keep money and food jobs separate.
Ask the adult if unsure. Use the agreed stop signal.

route_tasks.Supported: Work in an agreed quieter preparation role or use a tick-box order record; adult records help and your actual contribution.
route_tasks.Independent: Carry out your allocated role and check your own work within the adult’s supervision.
route_tasks.Aspire: Handle a customer’s change of order by checking it with the adult before any item or practice-money adjustment.

stages.stage: YOU DO record or clear down
stages.title: Clear down and ask for feedback
body: Close service when the adult directs.
Follow the adult’s put-away and cleaning plan.
Hand a feedback card to each customer.
Keep the actual order records.
A useful customer comment helps us improve.
stages.notes: 8 minutes. Second part of the source 18-minute You Do. Close and clear down under the approved food-safety plan. Do not keep or reuse food unless the adult confirms the actual storage/use instruction. Feedback cards may be offered as customers finish or during closing so departed customers are not invented. Obtain real comments with customer codes only. Record any help and uncompleted clean-down work.

stages.title: Count close and file
body: Count usable closing stock and practice cash.
Check against the actual records with the adult.
Keep feedback and your observation record.
Log your actual contribution and active minutes.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. VOC4-L2-E2 records actual counts and changes, with an explanation of any difference rather than a forced balance. File VOC4-L2-E1/E2/E3 in the evidence app. Planned time is 40 minutes, while actual active minutes remain blank until taught. Keep Careers minutes separate. No challenge-completion tick is automatic.

stages.title: Exit ticket
body: What did you contribute?
What did one customer actually say?
I helped by __. The comment was __.
My next step is __.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Private check using actual observation and feedback. Accept speech, signing, pointing or exact scribing. If there was no service or no customer comment, record that and the next step rather than supply a fictional comment.

support_pages.title: Opening and service prompt mat
lines: Two opening reminders: confirm the approved item and ingredient/allergen record with the adult; count the actual stock for your role.
Serve role: welcome; listen; record; repeat; pass the order; serve only after adult release; say thank you.
Prepare role: check the order with the adult; use the approved item; hand over the correct quantity; keep your station ready.

Keep practice-money handling and ready-to-eat food preparation in separate agreed roles. A person who touches practice money or a phone, cleans, handles waste or touches hair/face washes and dries hands again before food handling. The adult checks this before any role switch.
Stop signal: the adult agrees and practises it with you before opening. Ask for a quieter role or pause as agreed.
An allergy question or unclear ingredient stops the order for the responsible adult. Do not guess.
Customers are invited staff. Use customer codes, never names or contact details.

support_pages.title: Practice cold menu and order prompts
lines: Proposed training menu item: one adult-approved fruit pot. The proposed training price is £1 per pot, paid with practice money only.
The adult must confirm the actual menu, portion, ingredients/allergen information and practice price before opening. Do not assume the Theory item is still suitable to serve.
Order prompts: How many pots? I will repeat that. Is that right?
Tick-box access: one pot or two pots; record the actual approved item and amount. Ask the adult about any other quantity or change.
An unclear order: ask again. A change: confirm it with the adult before changing food or practice payment.
A complaint: listen calmly, apologise and ask the adult for an agreed next step.

support_pages.title: Stock count and feedback prompts
lines: Keep practice-money handling and ready-to-eat food preparation in separate agreed roles. A person who touches practice money or a phone, cleans, handles waste or touches hair/face washes and dries hands again before food handling. The adult checks this before any role switch.
Count each stock line at opening and closing using the same unit. Note stock added, used/served or set aside.
Worked training example only: opening 6 usable pots, added 0, used 2, held 0, usable closing 4.

Opening and closing stock mean usable items available for service, in the same unit. Held means set aside or discarded; it is separate and excluded. Count each item once as used or held, never both. Opening + added - used - held = usable closing. A difference needs checking; do not alter a real count to make it fit.
Ask a real customer: What worked? What could we improve? Use a customer code. A short comment is enough.
Do not fill in a model comment as actual feedback. If no comment was collected, record that and a next step.
Clear down by following the adult’s actual put-away and cleaning plan.

planner_sections.heading: Purpose and source
paragraphs: Exact outcome: Complete the allocated role during a supervised ten-minute café service for invited staff and collect feedback. Source: Medium Term Plan!D9; Lesson register!F13. Autumn 2 Week 4 Mission. No teaching date is inferred.

Run a supervised ten-minute cold-food café for invited staff, using allocated roles and practice payment only; then clear down and collect actual feedback. Each learner’s own observed contribution matters.

planner_sections.heading: Timing
paragraphs: Arrival 4; starter 2; I Do 5; We Do 5; You Do 18, split live service 10 and clear-down/feedback 8; tidy/file 4; exit 2. Total 40 minutes. Opening, outcome, vocabulary and hidden staff slide are untimed.

Record actual service start/finish and active lesson minutes. Ten minutes is planned, not a pre-filled performance record. If service is shortened or paused, record what happened and leave any unmet part clear.

paragraphs: Before food handling or opening, the responsible adult confirms the approved recipe and actual ingredient labels, written allergen information, clean suitable equipment and handwashing facilities, the agreed food-storage and service plan, the venue and supervision. planner_sections.heading: Menu practice money and handover
paragraphs: A proposed menu and worked practice-money example are supplied: one fruit pot at an authored training price of £1. The adult approves the actual menu, portions and practice price. No real payment or charge is taken.

Worked training float: one £2 coin, two £1 coins and two 50p coins total £5. One £1 item paid with £2 requires £1 change; net practice cash becomes £6. Actual float, sales and closing totals remain blank until counted. Model with empty pots before using approved actual food.

Handover: front-of-house takes and repeats the order; adult confirms and passes it to preparation; adult releases the approved item; learner serves as allocated and says thank you. Allergy or ingredient queries stop for the responsible adult to check written information.

planner_sections.heading: Learner roles and routes
paragraphs: Supported can take a quieter back-of-house role or use the tick-box record. Independent monitors their own allocated role within supervision. Aspire handles an order change only after checking it with the adult. Individual stations and adult-mediated handovers avoid forced pair work.

Do not require every learner to perform every café job. Record the allocated role and its real contribution. The actual order record may be kept by the agreed order-taker while the observer records preparation or handover contribution for another role.

planner_sections.heading: Stock clear down and feedback
paragraphs: Count actual opening and closing stock in the same unit. Record additions, used/served items and held/discarded items separately. Opening and closing counts mean usable stock available for service; held/discarded stock is excluded. Count each item once as used or held, never both. Opening + added - used - held should match usable closing; investigate a difference rather than force a match. Count practice cash before and after with actual sales and any authorised change recorded.

Use the eight-minute closing block for the adult’s storage, put-away and cleaning plan. Offer feedback cards while customers finish or at closing; do not invent comments from departed customers. Use customer codes only. No personal details are needed.

VOC4-L2-E3: real customer feedback, own contribution and a next step. Record support and actual time, with unperformed work left uncompleted.

staff_answers: Arrival: the supplied opening reminders are adult confirmation of the approved item/allergen information and an actual stock count. Accept two role-appropriate checks from the learner’s actual role card. Clear down means put away and clean under the adult’s plan. The actual stop signal is agreed and rehearsed individually before opening; do not assume a signal from an earlier lesson.

Readiness needs approved actual recipe/menu and ingredients, accurate written allergen information, suitable clean equipment and handwashing facilities, the storage/service plan, venue, supervision and invited staff. Do not open with any unresolved check. Empty-pot/card rehearsal is recorded as rehearsal and cannot establish the live-service outcome.

Practice money only. Worked float: £2 + £1 + £1 + 50p + 50p = £5. One £1 pot paid with £2 gives £1 change; net cash rises by £1 to £6. These are training values. The adult approves actual practice prices and records actual counted float, sales and closing cash separately.

Keep practice-money handling and ready-to-eat food preparation in separate agreed roles. A person who touches practice money or a phone, cleans, handles waste or touches hair/face washes and dries hands again before food handling. The adult checks this before any role switch.

Handover: take, record, repeat and confirm the order; pass through the adult to preparation; adult releases the approved item; serve in the allocated role and thank the customer. An uncertain ingredient/allergy question stops the order for the responsible adult. A complaint is heard calmly and referred for an agreed action.

Stock training example: opening 6 + added 0 - used 2 - held 0 = closing 4. Opening and closing actual counts mean usable items available for service, with the same unit. Held means set aside or discarded; it is recorded separately and excluded from the usable closing count. Count each item once as used or held, never both. Record genuine additions and set-aside items. Ask the adult to investigate any mismatch; do not adjust observed numbers to force a balance.

Ten-minute service plus eight-minute clear-down/feedback is the planned independent block. Actual start, finish, active minutes and each learner’s own role remain blank until observed. Record any shorter service or unperformed work accurately.

Feedback must come from an actual invited-staff customer using a code. Accept a brief comment and a realistic next step linked to the learner’s observed contribution. If no comment was collected, record that and the next step rather than substitute a model. No live-service outcome, qualification achievement or earned-time claim follows from a blank form or a planned duration.

proposed_recipe.status: Authored training example; adult approval required

sequence.detail: Wash thoroughly with liquid soap and warm running water, rinse and dry thoroughly. Ask the adult if help is needed.
Point to the two approved pre-cut fruits, amounts and clean pot. Do not start until the adult has confirmed the recipe.
The adult checks the actual ingredient labels, allergen information and storage plan. Do not guess or promise that food is safe.
Use the approved utensils. Weigh the approved amounts into one clean pot. No learner cutting is needed.
Keep the pot rim clean, fit the approved lid if used, and ask the adult where and how to store the item.
Deal with used utensils and surfaces under the adult’s instructions. Leave the area ready for the next task.

slides.title: The Mission
body: Run the café for invited staff
Use your role. Check, serve, clear down.
Open only when the adult says ready.
slides.notes: Untimed. Source: sources/MTP.xlsx; revision sha256:0895674f2901b602daf998b8a7aa1516522ce0c301b23bfba941fcc1807977cd. Medium Term Plan!D9; Lesson register!F13. This is a supervised real cold-food service with practice payment only. Before food handling or opening, the responsible adult confirms the approved recipe and actual ingredient labels, written allergen information, clean suitable equipment and handwashing facilities, the agreed food-storage and service plan, the venue and supervision. Hair is tied back, watches and jewellery are removed as required by the adult’s hygiene procedure, and phones stay away from the food area. The Mission also needs invited staff, approved cold items and practice money ready. Learners do not decide whether a food is suitable for an allergy. If any check is unresolved, do not prepare or serve that item: stop and refer to the responsible adult. Follow the setting’s food-safety procedures. Keep practice-money and food roles separate; wash and dry hands again before food handling after money, phones, cleaning, waste or touching hair/face. An unready session may rehearse with empty pots and cards, but must be recorded as rehearsal, not the completed practical or live-service outcome.

slides.title: Arrival task
body: Opening reminders: check with the adult; count stock.
Name your two opening checks.
What does clear down mean?
What is our agreed stop signal?
Why say thank you to a customer?
BLUE / GREEN / AMBER / RED. Choose a pause or quiet station.
slides.notes: 4 minutes. Self-contained reminders and role prompts are supplied. Check each learner’s actual role card without assuming previous teaching. Expected clear-down: put away and clean under the adult’s plan. The adult agrees and rehearses the actual stop signal with each learner individually before opening; no universal signal is assumed. Thank you acknowledges the customer politely. BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer a brief pause or quieter station without public disclosure. Agree one return action privately. The adult takes over any food task or service position while a learner pauses.

slides.title: Our service standard
body: Repeat each order before the handover.
Is that right?
Agree the stop signal with the adult.
If unsure, stop and ask.
slides.notes: 2 minutes. Revisit one concrete service standard: accurate repeat-back. Adult checks that each learner understands the locally agreed stop signal and the return action. Use the quieter preparation station if needed; do not require front-of-house performance.

slides.title: Today I can
body: Complete the allocated role during a supervised ten-minute café service for invited staff and collect feedback.
I can do my allocated role.
I can keep an accurate service record.
I can collect a useful customer comment.
slides.notes: Untimed. Exact source outcome. [QUAL] — agreed planner activity. The local checks do not replace the source outcome or invent official assessment wording.

slides.title: Check and hand over
body: Adult confirms safe opening.
Count stock and practice money.
Greet. Take the order. Repeat it.
Pass the order to the preparation station.
Adult releases the approved item. Say thank you.
slides.notes: 5 minutes. Model a complete handover through the adult, using an empty pot first. Then model practice payment only: the training example is one fruit pot at £1, paid with £2, change £1. slides.title: Run the opening checks
body: Confirm your actual role and two opening checks.
Count the actual opening stock.
Count the practice float together.
Rehearse the agreed stop signal.
Open only after the adult confirms readiness.
slides.notes: 5 minutes. Run checks together; record actual opening stock and float, not the worked example. Adult confirms the approved cold menu, ingredient/allergen record, storage/use plan, equipment, venue, invited staff and supervision. A fresh approved batch may be needed. Check actual item quantities and record them. Training float is £2 + £1 + £1 + 50p + 50p = £5, but actual values remain blank until counted. After counting practice money, wash and dry hands before handling food. Keep practice-money handling and ready-to-eat food preparation in separate agreed roles. A person who touches practice money or a phone, cleans, handles waste or touches hair/face washes and dries hands again before food handling. The adult checks this before any role switch.

slides.title: Ten-minute café service
body: Invited staff only. Keep to your agreed role.
Greet, repeat, hand over and serve as agreed.
Use the order record and practice money only. Keep money and food jobs separate.
Ask the adult if unsure. Use the agreed stop signal.
Supported: quieter station or tick-box record.
Aspire: check an order change with the adult.
slides.notes: 10 minutes. First part of the source 18-minute You Do. Record actual start and finish; ten minutes is the planned service window, not an automatic duration. Adult observes each learner’s own contribution and support on VOC4-L2-E1. Use actual customer codes and orders. Learner may use quiet back-of-house work; evidence must describe that real role rather than pretend they performed every role. If readiness is unresolved, do not open; label empty-pot/card rehearsal and leave live-service outcome uncompleted. route_tasks.Supported: Work in an agreed quieter preparation role or use a tick-box order record; adult records help and your actual contribution.
route_tasks.Independent: Carry out your allocated role and check your own work within the adult’s supervision.
route_tasks.Aspire: Handle a customer’s change of order by checking it with the adult before any item or practice-money adjustment.

slides.stage: YOU DO record or clear down
slides.title: Clear down and ask for feedback
body: Close service when the adult directs.
Follow the adult’s put-away and cleaning plan.
Hand a feedback card to each customer.
Keep the actual order records.
A useful customer comment helps us improve.
slides.notes: 8 minutes. Second part of the source 18-minute You Do. Close and clear down under the approved food-safety plan. Do not keep or reuse food unless the adult confirms the actual storage/use instruction. Feedback cards may be offered as customers finish or during closing so departed customers are not invented. Obtain real comments with customer codes only. Record any help and uncompleted clean-down work.

slides.title: Count close and file
body: Count usable closing stock and practice cash.
Check against the actual records with the adult.
Keep feedback and your observation record.
Log your actual contribution and active minutes.
slides.notes: 4 minutes. VOC4-L2-E2 records actual counts and changes, with an explanation of any difference rather than a forced balance. File VOC4-L2-E1/E2/E3 in the evidence app. Planned time is 40 minutes, while actual active minutes remain blank until taught. Keep Careers minutes separate. No challenge-completion tick is automatic.

slides.title: Exit ticket
body: What did you contribute?
What did one customer actually say?
I helped by __. The comment was __.
My next step is __.
slides.notes: 2 minutes. Private check using actual observation and feedback. Accept speech, signing, pointing or exact scribing. If there was no service or no customer comment, record that and the next step rather than supply a fictional comment.

slides.title: Key words
body: Role: your agreed job.
Hygiene: keep food and the work area clean.
Allergen: something that can cause an allergic reaction.
Stock: items ready to use or serve.
Float: practice money at the start.
Clear down: put away and clean.
Feedback: a useful comment.
slides.notes: Untimed reference. Refer to the real role card, stock line and feedback form. Only the responsible adult checks and authorises food-related decisions.

planner_sections.heading: Purpose and source
paragraphs: Exact outcome: Complete the allocated role during a supervised ten-minute café service for invited staff and collect feedback. Source: Medium Term Plan!D9; Lesson register!F13. Autumn 2 Week 4 Mission. No teaching date is inferred.

Run a supervised ten-minute cold-food café for invited staff, using allocated roles and practice payment only; then clear down and collect actual feedback. Each learner’s own observed contribution matters.

planner_sections.heading: Timing
paragraphs: Arrival 4; starter 2; I Do 5; We Do 5; You Do 18, split live service 10 and clear-down/feedback 8; tidy/file 4; exit 2. Total 40 minutes. Opening, outcome, vocabulary and hidden staff slide are untimed.

Record actual service start/finish and active lesson minutes. Ten minutes is planned, not a pre-filled performance record. If service is shortened or paused, record what happened and leave any unmet part clear.

planner_sections.heading: Before opening
paragraphs: Before food handling or opening, the responsible adult confirms the approved recipe and actual ingredient labels, written allergen information, clean suitable equipment and handwashing facilities, the agreed food-storage and service plan, the venue and supervision. Hair is tied back, watches and jewellery are removed as required by the adult’s hygiene procedure, and phones stay away from the food area. The Mission also needs invited staff, approved cold items and practice money ready. Learners do not decide whether a food is suitable for an allergy. If any check is unresolved, do not prepare or serve that item: stop and refer to the responsible adult. Follow the setting’s food-safety procedures. Keep practice-money and food roles separate; wash and dry hands again before food handling after money, phones, cleaning, waste or touching hair/face. An unready session may rehearse with empty pots and cards, but must be recorded as rehearsal, not the completed practical or live-service outcome.

Keep practice-money handling and ready-to-eat food preparation in separate agreed roles. A person who touches practice money or a phone, cleans, handles waste or touches hair/face washes and dries hands again before food handling. The adult checks this before any role switch.

Reconfirm actual roles, the locally agreed stop signal and two opening checks with every learner. Check any stored item against its actual approved storage/use plan; prepare fresh approved items when needed. Confirm invited-staff attendance in advance. An unready rehearsal is labelled and cannot prove this live-service outcome.

planner_sections.heading: Menu practice money and handover
paragraphs: A proposed menu and worked practice-money example are supplied: one fruit pot at an authored training price of £1. The adult approves the actual menu, portions and practice price. No real payment or charge is taken.

Worked training float: one £2 coin, two £1 coins and two 50p coins total £5. One £1 item paid with £2 requires £1 change; net practice cash becomes £6. Actual float, sales and closing totals remain blank until counted. Model with empty pots before using approved actual food.

Handover: front-of-house takes and repeats the order; adult confirms and passes it to preparation; adult releases the approved item; learner serves as allocated and says thank you. Allergy or ingredient queries stop for the responsible adult to check written information.

planner_sections.heading: Learner roles and routes
paragraphs: Supported can take a quieter back-of-house role or use the tick-box record. Independent monitors their own allocated role within supervision. Aspire handles an order change only after checking it with the adult. Individual stations and adult-mediated handovers avoid forced pair work.

Do not require every learner to perform every café job. Record the allocated role and its real contribution. The actual order record may be kept by the agreed order-taker while the observer records preparation or handover contribution for another role.

planner_sections.heading: Stock clear down and feedback
paragraphs: Count actual opening and closing stock in the same unit. Record additions, used/served items and held/discarded items separately. Opening and closing counts mean usable stock available for service; held/discarded stock is excluded. Count each item once as used or held, never both. Opening + added - used - held should match usable closing; investigate a difference rather than force a match. Count practice cash before and after with actual sales and any authorised change recorded.

Use the eight-minute closing block for the adult’s storage, put-away and cleaning plan. Offer feedback cards while customers finish or at closing; do not invent comments from departed customers. Use customer codes only. No personal details are needed.

planner_sections.heading: Evidence regulation and learner voice
paragraphs: VOC4-L2-E1: adult opening readiness, actual individual service observation and order record. VOC4-L2-E2: actual stock and practice-money records. VOC4-L2-E3: real customer feedback, own contribution and a next step. Record support and actual time, with unperformed work left uncompleted.

BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer a brief pause or quieter station without public disclosure. Agree one return action privately. The adult takes over any food task or service position while a learner pauses.

Use individual stations and agreed handovers through the responsible adult. No forced peer pair work, cold calling or class performance. Adults may read, rephrase and scribe exact words. They record prompts, actual actions and individual contribution; they do not invent observations or complete the learner’s choices. A plan, model or blank form is not completed evidence.

Lundy Space: agreed quieter role or pause. Voice: learner communicates role and check questions. Audience: adult observes and real customers comment. Influence: learner uses an actual comment to select an improvement. Use agreed local feedback codes. File genuine evidence in the evidence app.

paragraphs: The source plans this as [QUAL], an activity agreed with the tutor on the Plan sheet.
